extra.message: case_bundle_thaw_187() calls pickle.loads() on raw bytes taken directly from the request body (optionally base64-decoded from a GET param). pickle.loads on attacker-controlled data allows arbitrary object construction and remote code execution via crafted __reduce__ payloads.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: case_shell_probe_695() builds a shell command by concatenating the user-supplied 'host' GET parameter directly into os.system("ping -c 1 " + host). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. `; rm -rf /` or `$(cmd)`) to execute arbitrary commands.

cwe: CWE-78: OS Command Injection

extra.message: case_formula_cast_269() passes the user-supplied 'expr' GET parameter directly to eval(). Even with a restricted __builtins__ dict, Python eval sandboxes of this form are well known to be escapable (e.g. via ().__class__.__bases__ chains) allowing arbitrary code execution.

cwe: CWE-95: Eval Injection

extra.message: case_jinja_cast_686() concatenates the user-supplied 'fragment' GET parameter into a Jinja2 template string and renders it. This is a classic Server-Side Template Injection allowing arbitrary code execution via Jinja2 expressions (e.g. {{ self.__init__.__globals__ ... }}).

cwe: CWE-94: Code Injection

extra.message: case_xml_fold_736() parses the raw request body with an lxml XMLParser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True and no_network=False. An attacker-supplied XML document with an external/internal entity can read local files or trigger SSRF/DoS (billion laughs).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: case_mongo_lane_715() passes the parsed JSON request body (or its 'filter' key) directly as the MongoDB query filter to find_one() without validation. An attacker can inject operators like {"$where": ...} or {"$ne": null} to bypass query logic or execute server-side JS.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: case_client_fold_108() is the only ops endpoint that does not call _wrk_gate(request) before executing. It is reachable by any unauthenticated user and returns sensitive business data ('renewal risk, payment flags, owner contact details') and a case count.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: case_return_lane_164() redirects to the 'lane' value taken from GET/POST without validating it is a local/whitelisted URL. An attacker can craft a link to this endpoint pointing at an external phishing site.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: case_origin_mirror_665() reflects the client-supplied Origin header back in Access-Control-Allow-Origin and additionally sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows any external origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the response, defeating the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: case_frame_slip_675() explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' and empties the Content-Security-Policy header, weakening browser-side XSS mitigations for responses from this endpoint.

cwe: CWE-16: Configuration

extra.message: case_trust_drift_728() creates an unverified SSL context (ssl._create_unverified_context()) and uses it to fetch an HTTPS URL, disabling certificate validation and hostname verification. This exposes the request to man-in-the-middle attacks.

cwe: CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation

extra.message: case_identity_hint_655() checks a caller-supplied 'verifier' against hardcoded secret values in source ({'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'}) using a non-constant-time '!=' comparison. The secrets are embedded in code (visible to anyone with repo access) and the comparison is vulnerable to timing attacks.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: case_pulse_spill_352() deliberately raises a RuntimeError embedding the internal BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path and returns exc message/class in the JSON response body, leaking internal server file-system layout to the caller.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: case_wire_tally_228() logs the entire raw request body and the Authorization header value at WARNING level via logger.warning. Bearer tokens/credentials sent in that header are persisted in plaintext log files.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: case_blob_shelf_106() saves an uploaded file (or raw request body) to disk using an attacker-controlled name (drop_blob.name or the 'packet_ref' GET param) with no validation of file extension, content type, or size, allowing upload of arbitrary/dangerous file types into the server's storage.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: case_nonce_roll_705() generates a security-sounding 'code'/nonce using the non-cryptographic random.choice() (Mersenne Twister) instead of the secrets module. Such codes are predictable if the generator state is inferred, undermining their use as a nonce/token.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: case_trace_panel_745() returns the DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE environment variable and the internal BASE_EXPORT_DIR path in the JSON response, exposing internal configuration/deployment details.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: case_settlement_nudge_107() applies an arbitrary caller-supplied 'delta_value' to a case's approved financial amount, identified only by a caller-supplied 'case_id'. Beyond the shared internal-token gate, there is no check that the caller is authorized to modify that specific case's financials.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: case_spool_fan_315() builds an in-memory list sized by the caller-supplied 'count' GET parameter with no upper bound or type limit, allowing a caller to request an arbitrarily large response and exhaust server memory/CPU.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: api_matter_detail() only rejects clients; any authenticated attorney or paralegal can fetch any Matter by pk regardless of assignment, unlike the sibling api_matters() list view (and matters.views.can_access_matter used elsewhere) which correctly scope results to matters the user is assigned to. This is an IDOR allowing attorneys/paralegals to read matter titles/descriptions/sensitivity for cases they are not assigned to, including 'critical' sensitivity matters.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: client_message_send() only requires @login_required with no role/permission or matter-ownership check (unlike client_message_approve which requires can_approve_messages()). Any authenticated user, including a client account, can POST/GET this endpoint with an arbitrary ClientMessage pk and flip its status from 'approved' to 'sent', bypassing the intended attorney/paralegal approval-and-send workflow.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: export_matters_csv() writes user-controlled fields (matter.title, client.name, billing/free-text fields elsewhere) directly into CSV cells with no sanitization of leading formula characters (=, +, -, @). A matter/client created with a title like '=HYPERLINK(...)' or '=cmd|...' will execute as a formula when the exported CSV is opened in Excel/Sheets. The same pattern applies to export_deadlines_csv and export_documents_csv in this file.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: The 'seed' management command creates real, functional accounts (including a firm_admin) with the hardcoded, publicly-visible password 'Password123'. If this command is ever run against a production or shared/staging database, these become live default credentials.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
